questions.q: What does the frame clause (ROWS/RANGE BETWEEN ... AND ...) control?
options: Exactly which rows within the current partition are included in the window calculation, relative to the current row
The order in which partitions are evaluated
Whether the query uses an index
Which columns appear in the SELECT list
questions.explain: The frame clause narrows the window function's calculation to a specific set of rows around the current row, inside its partition.

questions.q: What does ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW count?
options: A fixed 3 physical rows: the 2 immediately before the current row, plus the current row itself
Every row with the same ORDER BY value as the current row
All rows in the entire partition
Only rows after the current row
questions.explain: ROWS counts physical row positions, always exactly 3 rows here, regardless of what values those rows contain.

questions.q: How does RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW differ from the ROWS equivalent when ORDER BY values are tied?
options: RANGE ignores ORDER BY entirely
RANGE includes every row that shares the current row's ORDER BY value, treating tied rows as one logical group
RANGE only works with PARTITION BY, never alone
RANGE and ROWS always produce identical results in every case
questions.explain: RANGE works on the logical ORDER BY value rather than physical position — tied rows are treated as peers and all included together.

questions.q: Why did the default frame from the FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE lesson cause LAST_VALUE to usually return the current row's own value?
options: PARTITION BY was missing from the query
The default frame uses RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, which only looks up to the current row's logical position
LAST_VALUE always ignores frames entirely
ROWS and RANGE behave identically in all cases
questions.explain: The default frame stops at the current row, so LAST_VALUE can never see past it unless an explicit ROWS frame covering the whole partition is used.

questions.q: As a general rule, when should RANGE be preferred over ROWS?
options: Never — RANGE is deprecated in SQL Server
Only when tied ORDER BY values should specifically be treated as one logical group
Always — RANGE should be the default choice for every window function
Only when PARTITION BY is omitted
questions.explain: ROWS is the predictable default for most calculations like running totals; RANGE is reserved for the specific case of grouping tied values together.
